/api/v1/projects/prj_plantwatertracker/f.title: Snooze a plant's due date
/api/v1/projects/prj_plantwatertracker/f.description:
Needs: Log waterings and keep history (the snooze must clear when a watering is logged).

From a home card and from the Plant detail page, the user can snooze a plant: push its due date by 1 day, or by a chosen number of days (e.g. the soil is still wet). Store this in the plant's snoozed_until field. The due helper uses the later of the normal due date and the snooze date, so the plant moves to the right group. Show 'Snoozed until <date>' on the plant, with a way to cancel the snooze. Logging a watering clears the snooze. Tests for the due calculation with a snooze and for clearing it.

Part of the project's vision as P1.1.
/api/v1/projects/prj_plantwatertracker/f.accepted_goal:
Let the user snooze a plant's watering due date when it doesn't need water yet (for example, the soil is still wet). From a plant's home card and from its Plant detail page (/plants/:id), the user can push the due date by 1 day with one tap, or by a chosen number of days. The snooze is stored in the plant's existing nullable snoozed_until column. The shared due-date helper in api/src then uses the later of the normal due date (newest watering + interval_days) and snoozed_until. That way the plant's status (overdue / due today / upcoming) and its days count are correct, and the home page shows it in the right group. While a snooze is in effect, the plant shows 'Snoozed until <date>' on its home card and on its detail page, with a way to cancel the snooze, which sets snoozed_until back to NULL. Logging a watering clears the snooze automatically. Add tests for the due calculation with a snooze and for clearing it, both by cancelling and by logging a watering.

Prerequisites: this work starts only after "Set up app shell, data model and catalog" and "Log waterings and keep history" have merged to main. Do NOT build the plant, due-date or watering pieces here; they already exist. Before planning, the lead must read the merged code on main and adapt to its actual names: table and column names, the due helper's name and signature, route and handler files, frontend components, the API client, and the test helpers. Expected on main: a plants table with a nullable snoozed_until column; a waterings table; a shared due-date helper in api/src that returns status plus days using local calendar dates; frontend routes / (Home, with cards grouped Overdue / Due today / Upcoming), /plants/new, /plants/:id and /plants/:id/edit; and POST /api/plants/:id/waterings, GET /api/plants/:id/waterings and DELETE /api/waterings/:id, with a Watered button on home cards and on the detail page.

Areas to touch:
- api/src due-date helper (whatever file Foundation creates): effective due = later of (newest watering + interval_days) and snoozed_until; status and days computed from the effective due date; expose whether a snooze is in effect and its date so the UI can show it
- api/src plant routes (in app.js or the router module Foundation adds): new endpoints to set a snooze (body: days, a positive integer) and to cancel it (set snoozed_until = NULL); return the updated plant with its recomputed due info, in the same shape the list and detail endpoints use
- api/src waterings route (POST /api/plants/:id/waterings from the Waterings work): also set the plant's snoozed_until = NULL in the same transaction that inserts the watering
- api/src plant list and detail serializers: include snoozed_until (and the snooze-in-effect flag, if added) in the responses Home and Detail already use
- api/src plant update handler (PUT/PATCH used by /plants/:id/edit): make sure editing a plant does not overwrite or drop snoozed_until unintentionally
- frontend home card component (Dashboard): a 'Snooze 1 day' action and a way to snooze N days; 'Snoozed until <date>' with a Cancel snooze control; refresh so the card moves to the right group
- frontend Plant detail page (/plants/:id): the same snooze controls, the 'Snoozed until <date>' display and cancel
- frontend API client module (whatever Foundation/Waterings use): functions for setting and cancelling a snooze
- api tests (Vitest + supertest with openDb(':memory:'), as in api/src/app.test.js and whatever later tests add): due helper with a snooze; set, cancel and validate endpoints; watering clears the snooze
- frontend tests (Vitest; currently renderToString in a node environment): rendering of 'Snoozed until <date>' and the snooze/cancel controls, following whatever pattern is on main by then
- README.md: brief mention of snoozing, if the README lists features by then

Worth planning around:
- Read main first. Today's main (9bfb1d3) is only the scaffold: Express 5 with createApp(db) in api/src/app.js, better-sqlite3 opened by openDb() in api/src/db.js with foreign_keys ON and WAL, and React 19 + Vite with no router or test DOM library. All the plant, watering and due-date code comes from the two prerequisite work orders. Use their real names, and do not re-create or duplicate those pieces.
- Schema: snoozed_until already exists, is nullable, and is created by Foundation, so no migration should be needed. Check its stored format (most likely a local calendar date string, YYYY-MM-DD) and use the same format. Store a date, not a timestamp, so comparisons with the helper's local-calendar-date logic stay consistent.
- Due rule: effective due date = max(normal due date, snoozed_until). Only a later snoozed_until changes anything. A snoozed_until in the past or before the normal due date has no effect, so the plant must not show as snoozed. Show 'Snoozed until <date>' only when snoozed_until is later than the normal due date (in practice this also means today or later). Keep this rule in the shared helper so Home grouping, the detail page and the API all agree; don't recompute it in the frontend.
- Check how the existing helper treats a plant with no waterings (for example due today, or based on a created date) and make sure a snooze extends that case the same way.
- Snooze base date (recommendation; see open questions): snoozed_until = max(today, current effective due date) + N days. Counting from the due date of an overdue plant would leave it still overdue, so 'snooze 1 day' would do nothing useful. Counting from the effective due date lets snoozes stack on an upcoming plant.
- Validation: days must be a positive integer within a sane upper bound (for example 1–365). Reject anything else with 400, using the API's existing error shape. Unknown plant id returns 404, matching the existing plant routes.
- Clearing on watering: set snoozed_until = NULL inside the same db.transaction as the watering insert in POST /api/plants/:id/waterings. better-sqlite3 transactions are synchronous. Clear it even if the watering is backdated, if the Waterings work allows backdating. Deleting a watering (DELETE /api/waterings/:id) should NOT restore a previous snooze; there's no history of snoozes.
- Plant edit: if the edit endpoint writes every column from the request body, make sure it keeps snoozed_until instead of setting it to NULL.
- Dates: the helper uses local calendar dates. Follow how Foundation computes 'today' (an injectable 'today' or clock parameter, if it has one) so tests are deterministic and don't depend on time zone or midnight. Format '<date>' in the UI the same way the rest of the app shows dates.
- UI: keep the calm, minimal style. On cards, '+1 day' should be one tap. The N-days choice can be a small number input or a few presets plus a custom value; avoid heavy modals. After setting or cancelling a snooze, refresh the data so the card moves between Overdue / Due today / Upcoming. Use real buttons with clear accessible labels.
- Tests required by the work order: (a) due helper cases: no snooze; snooze later than the normal due date (status and days follow the snooze, so an overdue plant moves to upcoming); snooze earlier than or equal to the normal due date (no effect); snooze in the past; null snoozed_until. (b) API: set a snooze for 1 and for N days, and the list/detail responses reflect it; cancel sets it to null; invalid days returns 400; unknown plant returns 404; POST watering clears snoozed_until. Also update any existing Foundation/Dashboard/Waterings tests whose expected response shape changes.
- Run tests with npm test at the repo root (Vitest in api/ and frontend/). Don't add new dependencies unless the existing test setup on main truly can't cover the UI.

Open questions to settle while planning:
- What date does a snooze count from? Recommended: max(today, current effective due date) + N days. The alternative, today + N, doesn't stack. Confirm against the existing helper's semantics.
- API shape: a dedicated snooze sub-resource (for example PUT/POST /api/plants/:id/snooze {days} and DELETE /api/plants/:id/snooze), or a PATCH on the plant. Pick whatever fits the route style on main.
- How the user picks N days on a card: a number input, presets (1/2/3/7) plus custom, or similar. Keep it small and consistent between the card and the detail page.

/api/v1/projects/prj_plantwatertracker/f.title: Show due count badge
/api/v1/projects/prj_plantwatertracker/f.description:
Needs: Log waterings and keep history (the badge must refresh after each watering).

In the header's reserved badge spot, show a badge with the number of plants that are due today or overdue. Hide it, or show it calmly, when that number is zero. It links to the home dashboard. It updates right after each watering, undo, plant change or deletion (e.g. through a shared refresh or context on the frontend), not only on reload. Optionally show the count in the document title too. Mobile-friendly.

Part of the project's vision as P1.3.
/api/v1/projects/prj_plantwatertracker/f.accepted_goal:
Add a "due count" badge to the Plant Water Tracker's app header, item P1.3 of the project vision. The badge sits in the header's reserved badge spot and shows how many plants are due today or overdue. It links to the home dashboard, so the user can glance at it from any page and jump to the plants that need water. When the count is zero, hide the badge or show it in a calm, muted style; never as an alarming "0" alert. The count must stay current without a page reload. It updates right after a watering is logged, a watering is undone, a plant is added or edited (for example, its interval changes), or a plant is deleted. Do this through one shared source of due state on the frontend (a React context/provider or a shared refresh function) that every mutating action calls. Do not poll, and do not let each page refetch on its own. Optionally, show the count in the document title too (e.g. "(3) Plant Water Tracker"), falling back to the plain title at zero. The badge must work well on mobile: a tap target of about 44px, no header overflow on narrow screens, and an accessible label such as "3 plants need water". It depends on the "Log waterings and keep history" feature, and on the plants and dashboard work before it, being on main.

Areas to touch:
- frontend/src/App.jsx (or the header/layout component the prerequisite work introduced): render the badge in the reserved header badge spot and wrap the app in the shared due-state provider
- new frontend module, e.g. frontend/src/DueContext.jsx (or extend an existing plants/data context if one exists): holds the due count, fetches it from the API and exposes refresh()
- new badge component, e.g. frontend/src/DueBadge.jsx: shows the count, has a calm or hidden zero state, links to the home dashboard and has an aria-label
- frontend watering, undo, plant create/edit and delete handlers (wherever the prerequisite features put them): call the shared refresh() after each successful mutation
- frontend/src/index.css: badge styles using the existing green palette variables, plus mobile sizing
- optionally a small effect that sets document.title from the count
- api/src/app.js: only if no existing endpoint already returns due status. Reuse the dashboard's due/overdue classification, or add a light endpoint such as GET /api/plants/due-count that uses the same logic
- tests: api/src/app.test.js (if an endpoint is added) and frontend tests for the badge and context

Worth planning around:
- Current state of main (checked): only a scaffold. api/src/app.js has just GET /api/health; db.js opens SQLite (better-sqlite3, WAL, foreign_keys ON) with no tables; frontend/src/App.jsx is a static start page with no header, no router and no badge spot. The plants table, the waterings/history feature, the dashboard, the header with its reserved badge spot, and any routing all come from earlier work orders. Before planning, confirm those have landed and use their actual names, endpoints and components. If they are missing, stop and report rather than build them here.
- There must be one definition of 'due today or overdue'. Use the same date/interval logic the dashboard uses (ideally a shared server-side function), so the badge and the dashboard always agree. Be careful about local versus UTC dates: 'today' should mean the user's local day, consistent with the dashboard.
- If the dashboard already fetches the full plant list with due status, the context can derive the count from that list instead of making an extra request. Either way, the dashboard and badge should share one refresh path so a watering updates both.
- Undo must also trigger refresh. So must deleting a plant, including any cascade that removes its waterings.
- The 'link to the home dashboard' should use whatever navigation the app already has: a router Link if a router exists, otherwise a plain anchor to '/'. Do not add a router just for this.
- Zero state: prefer hiding the badge, or a muted style without any red or warning colour, so it fits the 'calm, green-themed' tone in the README. While the count is loading or the request has failed, show nothing rather than a wrong number.
- Styling: reuse the CSS variables in frontend/src/index.css (--green-700, --green-100, etc.). The app has no CSS framework; plain CSS in index.css is the pattern.
- Testing setup (checked): Vitest in both packages. The API tests use supertest against createApp(openDb(':memory:')). The frontend tests run with environment: 'node' and use renderToString, and there is no jsdom or Testing Library. Pure functions and server rendering are the easy things to test. Testing that the badge refreshes after a mutation would need a DOM environment; if the agents add one (e.g. jsdom plus @testing-library/react as dev dependencies), they should keep it minimal and keep `npm test` at the root passing.
- Express 5 and React 19 are already pinned in package.json; don't change versions. The frontend calls only relative /api paths, which the Vite dev server proxies to the API.
- The document title in frontend/index.html is 'Plant Water Tracker'. If the title count is added, restore that exact title when the count is zero.

Open questions to settle while planning:
- Hide the badge at zero, or show a muted 'all watered' state? Pick whichever fits the header the prerequisite work built.

- Include the optional document-title count? Recommended if it's cheap.

/api/v1/projects/prj_plantwatertracker/f.title: Add plant photos
/api/v1/projects/prj_plantwatertracker/f.description:
Needs: Manage plants with catalog picker (its add and edit forms and detail page).

The user can upload, replace or remove one optional photo per plant from the Add and Edit plant pages. Accept common image types (JPEG, PNG, WebP, HEIC if feasible) up to about 10 MB. Store the files in the API's data volume (next to the SQLite database, e.g. a photos/ folder). Save the path in plants.photo_path and serve the files through the API. Replacing or removing a photo, or deleting the plant, deletes the old file. The photo appears as a small square thumbnail on home cards and larger on the Plant detail page, with a friendly leaf placeholder when there is none. Tests for upload, replace, remove and cleanup.

Part of the project's vision as P1.2.
/api/v1/projects/prj_plantwatertracker/f.accepted_goal:
Let the user attach one optional photo to each plant, so that their plants are easy to recognise in the Plant Water Tracker. On the Add plant and Edit plant pages the user can upload a photo, replace it or remove it. Accepted types are JPEG, PNG and WebP, plus HEIC/HEIF if that is feasible, up to about 10 MB. The API stores photo files in its data volume in a photos/ folder next to plants.db (DATA_DIR/photos). It records the file's relative path in a new nullable column, plants.photo_path, and serves the file over an /api route, so the Vite /api proxy covers it. Replacing or removing a photo deletes the old file from disk, and so does deleting the plant. The UI shows the photo as a small square thumbnail on home-page plant cards and larger on the Plant detail page. When a plant has no photo it shows a friendly leaf placeholder in the same spot, matching the existing 🌿 start-page style. Add API tests for upload, replace, remove and file cleanup (including on plant delete), plus frontend tests for the thumbnail/placeholder rendering. This builds on the "Manage plants with catalog picker" feature (plants table, plant CRUD routes, Add/Edit forms, detail page, home cards). That feature is not in main yet: main is only the scaffold. Fit into whatever structure it introduces.

Areas to touch:
- api/src/db.js: schema/migration adding nullable plants.photo_path TEXT (follow whatever migration approach the plants feature uses; it must also work on an existing DB that already has a plants table)
- api/src/app.js (or plant routes module from the dependency): photo upload/replace endpoint (multipart), remove endpoint, photo-serving GET route, file cleanup in plant DELETE; include photo URL or photo_path in plant JSON
- api/src/server.js: create DATA_DIR/photos and pass the photos directory into createApp (currently createApp(db) only)
- api/package.json + package-lock.json: add a multipart parser (e.g. multer), and optionally a HEIC converter
- api/src/*.test.js: tests for upload, replace, remove, rejects (wrong type/too big), serving, and cleanup on replace/remove/plant delete, using a temp photos dir
- frontend Add/Edit plant forms (from dependency): file input with preview, replace and remove controls, size/type validation messages; send the photo after or alongside the plant save
- frontend home plant card + Plant detail page: square thumbnail / larger image with leaf placeholder (a shared PlantPhoto component is a good fit)
- frontend/src/index.css: thumbnail/large photo/placeholder styles (object-fit: cover, square aspect)
- frontend tests: placeholder vs image rendering
- README.md: mention photos stored in api-data volume under photos/

Worth planning around:
- Repo state checked on main: api/src/app.js exports createApp(db) with only GET /api/health and express.json(); db.js openDb(filename) enables WAL and foreign_keys and skips mkdir for ':memory:'; server.js uses DATA_DIR (compose sets /app/data on the api-data named volume) and opens DATA_DIR/plants.db. No plants table, routes or pages exist yet, so rebase onto or wait for the catalog-picker feature.
- Stack: Express 5.3 (async handler errors reach the error handler automatically; no multipart parsing built in), better-sqlite3 13 (synchronous), React 19 + Vite 8, Vitest 5, supertest. There is no router, jsdom or testing-library: frontend tests use react-dom/server renderToString in a node environment. Follow that pattern unless the dependency feature changed it.
- Make the photos directory injectable (e.g. createApp(db, { photosDir })) so tests use a fresh fs.mkdtemp dir with ':memory:' DB and can assert files appear and disappear.
- Security: generate filenames on the server (random UUID + extension from the detected type) and never use the client filename. Store only the relative path (e.g. photos/<uuid>.jpg) in photo_path, and resolve and confirm it stays inside photosDir before reading or deleting. Detect type from magic bytes, not just Content-Type or extension. Serve with the correct Content-Type and X-Content-Type-Options: nosniff. Reject anything else with 400 and oversize files with 413 (multer LIMIT_FILE_SIZE needs mapping to a friendly JSON error).
- Ordering and consistency: on replace, write the new file, update the DB row, then delete the old file. If the DB update fails, delete the new file. If deleting the old file fails, log it and don't fail the request. Treat a missing file as already deleted (ENOENT is fine). On plant delete, read photo_path before deleting the row and unlink afterwards. If multer writes to disk, make sure a rejected upload or an unknown plant id leaves no stray file (memoryStorage + validate + write avoids this; 10 MB in memory is fine for a single-user app).
- Caching: photo filenames change on every replace, so a URL that includes the filename or a version (e.g. /api/plants/:id/photo?v=<uuid> or /api/photos/<uuid>.jpg) avoids showing a stale image after replace.
- Docker: compose only bind-mounts api/src, and node_modules come from npm ci in the image. Adding an npm dependency means updating package-lock.json and rebuilding (docker compose up --build), so note this in the README or PR. The photos live inside the existing api-data volume, so compose needs no change.
- HEIC: Chrome, Firefox and Edge cannot display HEIC; only Safari can. Storing HEIC as-is would show broken images on most browsers. Sharp's prebuilt binaries do not decode HEVC-based HEIC. A pure-JS converter (e.g. heic-convert/libheif-js) could turn HEIC into JPEG on upload, but it is slow and heavy. iOS Safari usually converts HEIC to JPEG itself when picking from the photo library with accept='image/*'.
- UI: thumbnail square via aspect-ratio: 1 + object-fit: cover. Use alt text with the plant name, and give the placeholder role='img' with an aria-label or an aria-hidden decorative label. Keep the calm green theme from index.css. File input accept='image/jpeg,image/png,image/webp,image/heic,image/heif'. Check size on the client too, for faster feedback, but the server stays authoritative.
- Add form: the plant does not exist until it is saved, so either upload after the create response returns the id, or accept multipart on create. Pick one and keep Edit consistent. Remove should be a distinct action (e.g. DELETE /api/plants/:id/photo or a 'remove' flag) and should not happen just because the file input was left empty.
- Existing test to keep passing: api/src/app.test.js health test calls createApp(openDb(':memory:')), so any new createApp options need defaults or that test must be updated.

Open questions to settle while planning:
- HEIC support: (a) convert HEIC/HEIF to JPEG on the server with a pure-JS converter, which adds a heavy dependency, (b) reject HEIC with a friendly message and rely on iOS converting to JPEG itself, or (c) store HEIC as-is, accepting that it won't display outside Safari. Recommended: (a) if the dependency is acceptable, otherwise (b). Avoid (c).
- API shape: multipart on plant create/update, or a separate PUT/DELETE /api/plants/:id/photo sub-resource? The sub-resource is simpler to test and keeps the JSON plant endpoints unchanged. Settle this against how the dependency feature's routes and forms are built.

/api/v1/projects/prj_plantwatertracker/f.title: Log waterings and keep history
/api/v1/projects/prj_plantwatertracker/f.description:
Needs: Set up app shell, data model and catalog (its waterings table and due helper).

Add a one-tap 'Watered' button on each home card and on the Plant detail page. It logs a watering for today, and the plant moves to the right due group at once. After tapping, show a short Undo prompt (toast) that removes that watering. On the detail page the user can also log a backdated watering by picking a past date (not a future one). The detail page shows the plant's watering history newest first, with a delete button on each entry to remove an accidental log. The next due date always comes from the newest remaining watering. API endpoints: POST /api/plants/:id/waterings (with an optional date), GET /api/plants/:id/waterings and DELETE /api/waterings/:id. Tests for the endpoints and the due recalculation.

Part of the project's vision as P0.4.
/api/v1/projects/prj_plantwatertracker/f.accepted_goal:
Let the user log waterings and keep a history for each plant in the Plant Water Tracker (a personal React/Vite + Express 5/SQLite app; vision item P0.4). Each plant card on the home screen and the Plant detail page gets a one-tap "Watered" button. It records a watering dated today, and the plant moves to the correct due group (overdue / due today / coming up) straight away, with no manual reload. After a tap, a short toast with "Undo" appears, and Undo deletes exactly that watering. On the detail page the user can also log a backdated watering by picking a past date (today or earlier, never a future date). The detail page lists the plant's watering history newest first, and each entry has a delete button to remove a log made by mistake. The next due date is always calculated from the newest remaining watering, by watered date and not by insertion order, so it stays correct after backdating, undo, or delete. API: POST /api/plants/:id/waterings (optional date in the body; defaults to today), GET /api/plants/:id/waterings (newest first), DELETE /api/waterings/:id. Add API tests for these endpoints and for the due recalculation.

Areas to touch:
- api/src/app.js: add the three waterings routes (or a waterings router mounted from createApp(db)), following the existing createApp(db) dependency-injection pattern
- api/src/db.js (or wherever the prerequisite puts schema/migrations): reuse the existing waterings table; add an index on (plant_id, watered_on) only if it is missing
- Due helper from the prerequisite: make sure it uses MAX(watered date) of the remaining waterings, and reuse it in the POST/DELETE responses so the client gets the plant's new due state
- api/src/*.test.js: new supertest + Vitest tests for the waterings endpoints and due recalculation, using openDb(':memory:')
- frontend home plant card component (from prerequisite): add the Watered button, then update or refetch the plant list so the card moves group at once
- frontend Plant detail page (from prerequisite): Watered button, backdate form (date input with max = today), history list newest first with a delete button per entry
- frontend: new small Toast/Undo component and shared state (e.g. in App) so the toast works from both home and detail views
- frontend API client module (if the prerequisite has one): add logWatering(plantId, date?), listWaterings(plantId), deleteWatering(id)

Worth planning around:
- Dependency: on main today (commit 9bfb1d3) only the scaffold exists. api/src/app.js has just GET /api/health, db.js only opens the DB (WAL, foreign_keys = ON), and App.jsx is a static start page with no router. The waterings table, due helper, plants API, home cards and detail page all come from the prerequisite work order. Before planning, read its actual schema (column names and date storage format), due-helper signature, and frontend structure; do not assume any of them.
- Dates: store and compare plain calendar dates as YYYY-MM-DD text. These sort correctly as strings, so ORDER BY watered_on DESC, id DESC gives newest first with a stable tie-break. Validate an optional `date` strictly: it must match the format and be a real calendar date (reject 2026-02-30 and the like). Return 400 for a malformed or future date.
- Timezone: 'today' should be the user's local date. The API container probably runs in UTC. To avoid off-by-one problems near midnight, the frontend should send its local today's date explicitly, even for the one-tap button; the server default (no date) is a fallback. The server's future-date check should allow at least the client's local today (e.g. reject only dates after server today + 1 day, or document the chosen rule).
- Error handling: unknown plant on POST/GET → 404; unknown watering id on DELETE → 404; successful DELETE → 204 (or 200 with the updated plant due state, if the UI needs it). Express 5 forwards rejected async handlers to error middleware automatically; better-sqlite3 is synchronous.
- Undo must delete the specific watering id returned by POST, not 'the latest watering'. More than one watering on the same day is allowed, so ids are the identity.
- Due recalculation: after deleting the newest watering, the due date falls back to the next-newest one. If no waterings remain, use whatever 'never watered' behaviour the prerequisite's due helper defines. Backdating a watering older than the current newest must not change the due date. Cover all of these in tests.
- Foreign keys are ON. Check that the prerequisite's waterings.plant_id references plants with ON DELETE CASCADE (or that plant deletion handles waterings), but do not change plant-deletion behaviour in this work.
- Immediate regrouping: either have POST/DELETE return the updated plant (with next due date and group), or refetch the plant list. Either way, compute grouping in one place, the shared due helper, so client and server do not drift.
- Toast: one toast at a time; a new tap replaces the previous one. Auto-dismiss after a few seconds (about 5). Undo calls DELETE /api/waterings/:id, then refreshes the affected views. If the user goes from home to detail while the toast is showing, Undo should still work.
- Backdate input: <input type="date" max={localToday}>, plus server-side validation, because the max attribute is not enforced on submit in every browser.
- Testing: the API uses Vitest 5 + supertest against createApp(openDb(':memory:')); follow api/src/app.test.js. Frontend tests run in a 'node' environment with renderToString only (frontend/vite.config.js, App.test.jsx) and have no jsdom or testing-library, so keep frontend tests to render checks unless a devDependency is deliberately added. The existing App.test.jsx asserts 'Plant Water Tracker' appears; keep it passing. Root `npm test` runs both packages.
- Style: keep the app calm and green (frontend/src/index.css). Buttons need accessible labels that include the plant name (e.g. aria-label "Mark Monstera as watered").

- **better-sqlite3 behaviour.** It is synchronous. Wrap 'insert plant + insert first watering' in db.transaction() so a failure leaves neither row. Use prepared statements with bound parameters only. For idempotency, use CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS plus a version check (PRAGMA user_version is the simplest), so future migrations (later P0 items such as photos and snooze) can be appended.
- **Express 5 behaviour.** Rejected promises and thrown errors in handlers reach the error middleware automatically. express.json() raises a 400-type error on malformed JSON, so add a final error handler that answers with JSON ({error: message}) rather than Express's HTML page. /api/v1/projects/prj_plantwatertracker/f.description:
Set this new project up so work can start on it.

What the app is: Plant Water Tracker is a small personal web app for one person who wants to keep their houseplants alive without remembering every schedule. It ships with about 30 common houseplants, each with a typical watering interval and a care tip, so adding a plant fills in its schedule. The user can still adjust it. The home screen shows at a glance which plants are overdue, due today or coming up. One tap logs a watering, and each plant keeps its own watering history. It should become a calm, friendly, green-themed helper that works well in a narrow window. Its data is stored on the user's own computer and survives restarts, with no accounts, outside services or notifications.

Stack: Node.js LTS, built with React with Vite; Express with SQLite (better-sqlite3).

- Scaffold a minimal app on this stack that starts and shows a simple start page. Build none of the app's features yet; later work orders do that.
- Set up the stack's usual test runner with one passing test, so later work orders have a test command.
- Add a .gitignore for the stack and a README saying what the app is and that `docker compose up` runs it.
- Add the compose file for Commitarium's preview:

- Put one compose file at the repository root (compose.yaml), with one service per part the app needs (for example frontend, API, database). Servers listen on 0.0.0.0. The app opens over plain http://127.0.0.1 in a WebKit window that frames it, where Secure cookies are dropped; Commitarium sets COMMITARIUM_PREVIEW=1 in every preview container. When it is set, sign-in cookies must work over plain http (SameSite=Lax, not Secure, no __Host- or __Secure- names); production keeps its own settings.
- Run the app for development with live reload: start dev servers that reload on change (for example Vite's dev server, uvicorn --reload, nodemon) and bind-mount the source folders they watch (for example ./frontend/src:/app/src). Do not mount over dependency folders such as node_modules.
- Keep data in named volumes.
- Bind mounts, build contexts, and Dockerfiles stay inside the repository. No privileged mode, host networking, added capabilities, devices, secrets, env_file, or external volumes or networks. Every environment variable has an explicit value.
- The frontend reaches the API through a relative-path dev proxy (for example /api), not a hardcoded localhost port.
- Publish the port the user opens in a browser, and name it at the top level of the compose file:
  x-commitarium-preview:
    service: <the service the user opens>
    port: <its container port>

actions.title: Set up app shell, data model and catalog
actions.description:
Foundation for the Plant Water Tracker (React/Vite frontend in frontend/, Express 5 + better-sqlite3 API in api/, SQLite in the api-data named volume).

Outcome:
- A calm, friendly, mobile-friendly app shell with a green, plant-themed accent that works well in a narrow window. The header has the app name and a reserved spot for a due-count badge (filled in later). Add client-side routes for Home (/), Add plant (/plants/new), Plant detail (/plants/:id) and Edit plant (/plants/:id/edit). Each is a placeholder page with clear spots for its later features. Keep the existing /api relative-path proxy.
- Database schema with simple, idempotent migrations run on API start: plants (id, name, species_key nullable, location, interval_days, notes, care_tip nullable, photo_path nullable, snoozed_until nullable, created_at, updated_at) and waterings (id, plant_id with ON DELETE CASCADE, watered_on date, created_at). The plant's last watering is its newest watering. Adding a plant later creates its first watering at the chosen date (default today).
- A shared, tested due-date helper in the API: next due = last watering date + interval_days (later pushed by snoozed_until when set). Return status (overdue, due today, upcoming) and days overdue or days left. Use local calendar dates, not timestamps.
- Basic JSON API: list plants with computed next_due, status and days; get one plant; create, update and delete plants with validation (name required, interval 1 to 365 days). GET /api/catalog returns the catalog.
- Read-only built-in catalog kept in code (e.g. api/src/catalog.json). Each entry has a key, common name, botanical name, default interval in days and a one-line care tip. Every tip also ends by saying to water less often in winter. Plants copy the interval and tip when created, so editing a plant never changes the catalog. Entries (common name, botanical name, interval, tip):
1 Pothos (Epipremnum aureum), 8: water when the top half of the soil is dry; drooping leaves mean it's thirsty.
2 Snake plant (Dracaena trifasciata), 18: let the soil dry out completely; overwatering is the main risk.
3 ZZ plant (Zamioculcas zamiifolia), 18: let the soil dry out completely; it stores water in its rhizomes.
4 Spider plant (Chlorophytum comosum), 7: keep lightly moist; water when the top 2–3 cm is dry.
5 Peace lily (Spathiphyllum), 7: water when the top 2–3 cm is dry; it droops visibly when thirsty.
6 Monstera (Monstera deliciosa), 9: water when the top 5 cm is dry.
7 Fiddle leaf fig (Ficus lyrata), 9: water when the top 5 cm is dry; dislikes soggy soil and being moved.
8 Rubber plant (Ficus elastica), 10: water when the top 5 cm is dry.
9 Heartleaf philodendron (Philodendron hederaceum), 8: water when the top 2–3 cm is dry.
10 Aloe vera (Aloe barbadensis miller), 21: soak, then let the soil dry out completely.
11 Jade plant (Crassula ovata), 18: let the soil dry out completely between waterings.
12 Chinese evergreen (Aglaonema), 10: water when the top 2–3 cm is dry.
13 Dracaena (Dracaena fragrans / marginata), 12: water when the top half of the soil is dry; sensitive to fluoride in tap water.
14 Boston fern (Nephrolepis exaltata), 3: keep the soil evenly moist; likes humidity.
15 English ivy (Hedera helix), 7: water when the top 2–3 cm is dry.
16 Calathea (Calathea / Goeppertia), 6: keep evenly moist, never soggy; prefers filtered or rainwater.
17 Prayer plant (Maranta leuconeura), 6: keep evenly moist; likes humidity.
18 Parlor palm (Chamaedorea elegans), 8: water when the top 2–3 cm is dry.
19 Areca palm (Dypsis lutescens), 7: keep lightly moist; water when the top 2–3 cm is dry.
20 Peperomia (Peperomia spp.), 10: let the top half dry out; its leaves store water.
21 Moth orchid (Phalaenopsis), 7: water when the bark or moss is almost dry; never leave it standing in water.
22 Cast iron plant (Aspidistra elatior), 14: let the top half dry out; very forgiving.
23 Echeveria and other rosette succulents, 14: soak, then let the soil dry out completely.
24 Cactus (various), 28: soak, then let the soil dry out completely; water very little in winter.
25 Bird of paradise (Strelitzia reginae), 8: water when the top 5 cm is dry.
26 String of pearls (Curio rowleyanus), 14: let the soil dry almost completely.
27 Hoya (Hoya carnosa), 12: let the soil dry out mostly; thick leaves store water.
28 African violet (Saintpaulia), 6: keep lightly moist; water from below and keep water off the leaves.
29 Money tree (Pachira aquatica), 12: water when the top half of the soil is dry.
30 Croton (Codiaeum variegatum), 6: keep lightly moist; water when the top 2–3 cm is dry.

actions.title: Set up app shell, data model and catalog
actions.description:
Lay the foundation for the Plant Water Tracker, a calm single-user houseplant watering app with no accounts and no cookies. The frontend is React/Vite in frontend/. The API is Express 5 + better-sqlite3 in api/, and the database is SQLite in the api-data Docker volume. This is P0.1 in the project vision; later work builds the real Home list, Add/Edit forms, watering log, snooze, photos and the due-count badge on top of it.

Deliver:
1. **App shell.** Mobile-first, works in a narrow window, calm and friendly, with a green plant-themed accent (extend the existing CSS variables in frontend/src/index.css). The header shows the app name "Plant Water Tracker" and keeps an empty placeholder spot for a due-count badge that a later feature fills in. Add client-side routes: Home (/), Add plant (/plants/new), Plant detail (/plants/:id) and Edit plant (/plants/:id/edit), plus a friendly not-found fallback. Each route is a placeholder page that clearly marks where its later features go. The browser keeps calling the API only through relative /api paths via the existing Vite proxy. English UI.
2. **Schema and migrations.** Simple, idempotent migrations run automatically when the API starts.
   - plants: id, name, species_key (nullable), location, interval_days, notes, care_tip (nullable), photo_path (nullable), snoozed_until (nullable), created_at, updated_at.
   - waterings: id, plant_id referencing plants with ON DELETE CASCADE, watered_on (YYYY-MM-DD local calendar date), created_at.
   - A plant's last watering is its newest waterings row (latest watered_on). Creating a plant also creates its first watering on a chosen date, defaulting to today.
3. **Due-date helper.** A pure, shared, unit-tested helper in the API, using local calendar dates rather than timestamps.
   - next_due = last watered_on + interval_days. If snoozed_until is set and later than that, the due date moves to snoozed_until (snooze itself is a later feature, but the helper supports it now).
   - Returns status 'overdue', 'due_today' or 'upcoming', plus days overdue or days left.
4. **JSON API.**
   - GET /api/plants lists plants, each with last_watered_on, next_due, status and days.
   - GET /api/plants/:id returns one plant with the same computed fields; 404 when it does not exist.
   - POST /api/plants creates a plant. PUT or PATCH /api/plants/:id updates one. DELETE /api/plants/:id deletes one, and its waterings cascade away.
   - Validation: name is required (non-blank after trimming); interval_days must be an integer from 1 to 365. Return 400 with a clear JSON error message.
   - GET /api/catalog returns the built-in catalog.
5. **Read-only catalog.** Kept in code, for example api/src/catalog.json. It holds exactly the 30 entries in the list below, each with a stable key (for example a slug such as 'pothos' or 'snake-plant'), common name, botanical name, default interval in days, and a one-line care tip. Every tip ends by saying to water less often in winter. When a plant is created from a species_key, it copies the catalog's interval and tip into its own interval_days and care_tip. Editing the plant only changes the plant, never the catalog.

Catalog entries (common name, botanical name, interval in days: tip):
1 Pothos (Epipremnum aureum), 8: water when the top half of the soil is dry; drooping leaves mean it's thirsty.
2 Snake plant (Dracaena trifasciata), 18: let the soil dry out completely; overwatering is the main risk.
3 ZZ plant (Zamioculcas zamiifolia), 18: let the soil dry out completely; it stores water in its rhizomes.
4 Spider plant (Chlorophytum comosum), 7: keep lightly moist; water when the top 2–3 cm is dry.
5 Peace lily (Spathiphyllum), 7: water when the top 2–3 cm is dry; it droops visibly when thirsty.
6 Monstera (Monstera deliciosa), 9: water when the top 5 cm is dry.
7 Fiddle leaf fig (Ficus lyrata), 9: water when the top 5 cm is dry; dislikes soggy soil and being moved.
8 Rubber plant (Ficus elastica), 10: water when the top 5 cm is dry.
9 Heartleaf philodendron (Philodendron hederaceum), 8: water when the top 2–3 cm is dry.
10 Aloe vera (Aloe barbadensis miller), 21: soak, then let the soil dry out completely.
11 Jade plant (Crassula ovata), 18: let the soil dry out completely between waterings.
12 Chinese evergreen (Aglaonema), 10: water when the top 2–3 cm is dry.
13 Dracaena (Dracaena fragrans / marginata), 12: water when the top half of the soil is dry; sensitive to fluoride in tap water.
14 Boston fern (Nephrolepis exaltata), 3: keep the soil evenly moist; likes humidity.
15 English ivy (Hedera helix), 7: water when the top 2–3 cm is dry.
16 Calathea (Calathea / Goeppertia), 6: keep evenly moist, never soggy; prefers filtered or rainwater.
17 Prayer plant (Maranta leuconeura), 6: keep evenly moist; likes humidity.
18 Parlor palm (Chamaedorea elegans), 8: water when the top 2–3 cm is dry.
19 Areca palm (Dypsis lutescens), 7: keep lightly moist; water when the top 2–3 cm is dry.
20 Peperomia (Peperomia spp.), 10: let the top half dry out; its leaves store water.
21 Moth orchid (Phalaenopsis), 7: water when the bark or moss is almost dry; never leave it standing in water.
22 Cast iron plant (Aspidistra elatior), 14: let the top half dry out; very forgiving.
23 Echeveria and other rosette succulents, 14: soak, then let the soil dry out completely.
24 Cactus (various), 28: soak, then let the soil dry out completely; water very little in winter.
25 Bird of paradise (Strelitzia reginae), 8: water when the top 5 cm is dry.
26 String of pearls (Curio rowleyanus), 14: let the soil dry almost completely.
27 Hoya (Hoya carnosa), 12: let the soil dry out mostly; thick leaves store water.
28 African violet (Saintpaulia), 6: keep lightly moist; water from below and keep water off the leaves.
29 Money tree (Pachira aquatica), 12: water when the top half of the soil is dry.
30 Croton (Codiaeum variegatum), 6: keep lightly moist; water when the top 2–3 cm is dry.

Tests: due helper, migrations (they create the schema, are safe to run twice, and cascade deletes work) and the API endpoints. `npm test` at the repo root must stay green.

**Where it changes**
- api/src/db.js: run migrations from openDb() (or from a migrate(db) it calls), so both server.js and the in-memory test DBs get the schema
- api/src/migrations.js (new): ordered, idempotent migration list tracked with PRAGMA user_version or a schema_migrations table; creates the plants and waterings tables and an index on waterings(plant_id, watered_on)
- api/src/due.js (new) + due.test.js: pure date helpers (today as a local YYYY-MM-DD string, add days, difference in days) and computeDue({lastWateredOn, intervalDays, snoozedUntil}, today) returning next_due, status and days
- api/src/catalog.json (new) + a small loader/lookup module: the 30 read-only entries
- api/src/app.js: plants CRUD routes, GET /api/catalog, validation, 404 handling and a JSON error handler (including malformed JSON bodies); keep /api/health
- api/src/app.test.js (and/or new plants.test.js, migrations.test.js): extend the existing supertest style that uses openDb(':memory:')
- frontend/src/App.jsx: becomes the layout (header with app name, empty due-badge slot, <Outlet/> or equivalent) plus the route table
- frontend/src/pages/ (new): Home, AddPlant, PlantDetail, EditPlant and NotFound placeholder pages with clearly labelled spots for later features
- frontend/src/main.jsx: wrap the app in the router provider if a router library is used
- frontend/src/index.css: shell layout, header, narrow-width styles; reuse the existing --green-* variables
- frontend/src/App.test.jsx: update for the routed shell (render each route, assert the heading and the badge slot)
- frontend/package.json + package-lock.json: only if a router dependency is added
- README.md: briefly document the API endpoints and the catalog

**To keep in mind**
- **API current state.** api/src/app.js exports createApp(db), which only has express.json() and GET /api/health. api/src/db.js openDb(filename) already sets journal_mode=WAL and foreign_keys=ON. foreign_keys is per-connection, and ON DELETE CASCADE depends on it, so keep it in openDb and test the cascade. The existing test calls createApp(openDb(':memory:')); putting migrations inside openDb keeps that pattern working and gives every test a fresh schema.
- **better-sqlite3 behaviour.** It is synchronous. Wrap 'insert plant + insert first watering' in db.transaction() so a failure leaves neither row. Use prepared statements with bound parameters only. For idempotency, use CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS plus a version check (PRAGMA user_version is the simplest), so future migrations (later P0 items such as photos and snooze) can be appended.
- **Express 5 behaviour.** Rejected promises and thrown errors in handlers reach the error middleware automatically. express.json() raises a 400-type error on malformed JSON, so add a final error handler that answers with JSON ({error: message}) rather than Express's HTML page. Parse :id as a positive integer and return 404 for unknown or non-numeric ids.
- **Dates and timezone.** Store watered_on, snoozed_until and next_due as 'YYYY-MM-DD' strings. Do day arithmetic on the calendar parts (for example Date.UTC(y, m-1, d) plus whole days), never by adding 86400000 ms to local timestamps, which breaks across DST. 'Today' comes from the local clock formatted as Y-M-D, not toISOString(), which is UTC. Let route handlers and computeDue accept an injectable 'today' so tests are deterministic. The API container has no TZ set, so its local time is UTC (see open questions).
- **Due status semantics.** next_due < today → overdue, with days = days overdue (positive). next_due == today → due_today, days = 0. Otherwise upcoming, with days = days left. Effective due = max(last + interval, snoozed_until) when snoozed_until is set. Pick one clear field shape (e.g. `days_overdue` / `days_left`, or a single `days` field plus status) and use it consistently, because the Home list and badge will consume it. Test the boundaries: interval 1, due exactly today, a month/year rollover, a leap day, and a snooze earlier vs later than the computed due date.
- **Plants with no waterings.** The data model allows a plant with no waterings (e.g. inserted directly, or if a later feature deletes waterings), even though POST always creates one. Handle it gracefully, for example by falling back to the plant's created date, or a null next_due with a defined status, and do not crash.
- **POST /api/plants input.** name (required, trimmed); optional species_key (must exist in the catalog, else 400); interval_days (integer 1–365; default the catalog interval when species_key is given and the interval is omitted; required otherwise); care_tip (default the catalog tip when species_key is given); location and notes (optional strings, stored as ''); and an optional first-watering date (e.g. last_watered_on, a valid YYYY-MM-DD, default today, probably not in the future). Return 201 with the created plant including computed fields. Reject non-integers, strings like '7abc', 0, and 366. Do not let clients set id, created_at, photo_path or snoozed_until through this endpoint unless deliberately designed.
- **Catalog contract.** GET /api/catalog returns all 30 entries in a stable order, with stable unique keys and camelCase or snake_case fields; match whatever style the plants API uses. The winter clause should read naturally on every tip, e.g. append ' Water less often in winter.' Entry 24 (Cactus) already says 'water very little in winter'; decide whether it still gets the suffix (the requirement says every tip ends with it), and avoid an awkward double. Add a test that asserts 30 entries, unique keys, intervals between 1 and 365, and every tip ending with the winter sentence.
- **Frontend has no router.** The only frontend dependencies are react/react-dom 19.3.1, with vite 8 and vitest 5. Docker images run `npm ci` at build time and compose mounts only ./frontend/src, so adding a dependency (e.g. react-router) means updating package.json and package-lock.json, and anyone using compose must rebuild (`docker compose up --build`). Versions in the repo are exact pins; follow that. A tiny in-house history router is an acceptable alternative.
- **Frontend tests.** They run with environment 'node' and use react-dom/server renderToString; there is no jsdom or testing-library. Route-level tests can render the router at a given URL (e.g. a static/memory router) to a string. Keep the existing 'Plant Water Tracker' heading assertion meaningful.
- **Vite proxy.** frontend/vite.config.js proxies /api to API_PROXY_TARGET. Keep it unchanged and keep all fetches relative ('/api/...'). Deep links like /plants/3 already fall back to index.html on the Vite dev server. Placeholder pages may call the API (e.g. Home lists plant names, detail fetches one plant), but that is optional in this item and must handle errors calmly.
- **Styling.** index.css has --green-900/700/100 and --bg, system font, and a centered .start block with max-width 28rem. Use a single narrow column, a sticky or simple header, comfortable tap targets (around 44px), and visible focus styles; no UI framework is needed. index.html already sets theme-color #2f6b3c and lang=en.
- **Privacy.** No cookies, sessions or auth. The README notes that any future cookies must be SameSite=Lax and not Secure under COMMITARIUM_PREVIEW=1. Nothing in this item should set cookies.
- **Data hygiene.** .gitignore already ignores data/ and *.db. Tests must use ':memory:' (or temp files that get cleaned up) and never the api-data volume path.

**Left to settle**
- Which 'local' timezone defines today? The API container runs in UTC unless TZ is set. Options: add a TZ setting to the api service in compose.yaml (e.g. TZ from the host or a configurable env var), or let the client pass its local date (e.g. ?today=YYYY-MM-DD) to the list and get endpoints. Pick one and document it.
- Router: add react-router (pinned, with lockfile updated and the Docker rebuild noted) or write a minimal in-house router? Either is fine; choose the one that keeps tests simple.
- Update verb: PUT (full replace) or PATCH (partial)? Decide which fields an update accepts (name, location, interval_days, notes, care_tip, species_key?), and whether changing species_key re-copies catalog defaults. The requirement only says edits never change the catalog.

actions.title: Snooze a plant's due date
actions.description:
Let the user snooze a plant's watering due date when it doesn't need water yet (for example, the soil is still wet). From a plant's home card and from its Plant detail page (/plants/:id), the user can push the due date by 1 day with one tap, or by a chosen number of days. The snooze is stored in the plant's existing nullable snoozed_until column. The shared due-date helper in api/src then uses the later of the normal due date (newest watering + interval_days) and snoozed_until. That way the plant's status (overdue / due today / upcoming) and its days count are correct, and the home page shows it in the right group. While a snooze is in effect, the plant shows 'Snoozed until <date>' on its home card and on its detail page, with a way to cancel the snooze, which sets snoozed_until back to NULL. Logging a watering clears the snooze automatically. Add tests for the due calculation with a snooze and for clearing it, both by cancelling and by logging a watering.

Prerequisites: this work starts only after "Set up app shell, data model and catalog" and "Log waterings and keep history" have merged to main. Do NOT build the plant, due-date or watering pieces here; they already exist. Before planning, the lead must read the merged code on main and adapt to its actual names: table and column names, the due helper's name and signature, route and handler files, frontend components, the API client, and the test helpers. Expected on main: a plants table with a nullable snoozed_until column; a waterings table; a shared due-date helper in api/src that returns status plus days using local calendar dates; frontend routes / (Home, with cards grouped Overdue / Due today / Upcoming), /plants/new, /plants/:id and /plants/:id/edit; and POST /api/plants/:id/waterings, GET /api/plants/:id/waterings and DELETE /api/waterings/:id, with a Watered button on home cards and on the detail page.

**Where it changes**
- api/src due-date helper (whatever file Foundation creates): effective due = later of (newest watering + interval_days) and snoozed_until; status and days computed from the effective due date; expose whether a snooze is in effect and its date so the UI can show it
- api/src plant routes (in app.js or the router module Foundation adds): new endpoints to set a snooze (body: days, a positive integer) and to cancel it (set snoozed_until = NULL); return the updated plant with its recomputed due info, in the same shape the list and detail endpoints use
- api/src waterings route (POST /api/plants/:id/waterings from the Waterings work): also set the plant's snoozed_until = NULL in the same transaction that inserts the watering
- api/src plant list and detail serializers: include snoozed_until (and the snooze-in-effect flag, if added) in the responses Home and Detail already use
- api/src plant update handler (PUT/PATCH used by /plants/:id/edit): make sure editing a plant does not overwrite or drop snoozed_until unintentionally
- frontend home card component (Dashboard): a 'Snooze 1 day' action and a way to snooze N days; 'Snoozed until <date>' with a Cancel snooze control; refresh so the card moves to the right group
- frontend Plant detail page (/plants/:id): the same snooze controls, the 'Snoozed until <date>' display and cancel
- frontend API client module (whatever Foundation/Waterings use): functions for setting and cancelling a snooze
- api tests (Vitest + supertest with openDb(':memory:'), as in api/src/app.test.js and whatever later tests add): due helper with a snooze; set, cancel and validate endpoints; watering clears the snooze
- frontend tests (Vitest; currently renderToString in a node environment): rendering of 'Snoozed until <date>' and the snooze/cancel controls, following whatever pattern is on main by then
- README.md: brief mention of snoozing, if the README lists features by then

**To keep in mind**
- Read main first. Today's main (9bfb1d3) is only the scaffold: Express 5 with createApp(db) in api/src/app.js, better-sqlite3 opened by openDb() in api/src/db.js with foreign_keys ON and WAL, and React 19 + Vite with no router or test DOM library. All the plant, watering and due-date code comes from the two prerequisite work orders. Use their real names, and do not re-create or duplicate those pieces.
- Schema: snoozed_until already exists, is nullable, and is created by Foundation, so no migration should be needed. Check its stored format (most likely a local calendar date string, YYYY-MM-DD) and use the same format. Store a date, not a timestamp, so comparisons with the helper's local-calendar-date logic stay consistent.
- Due rule: effective due date = max(normal due date, snoozed_until). Only a later snoozed_until changes anything. A snoozed_until in the past or before the normal due date has no effect, so the plant must not show as snoozed. Show 'Snoozed until <date>' only when snoozed_until is later than the normal due date (in practice this also means today or later). Keep this rule in the shared helper so Home grouping, the detail page and the API all agree; don't recompute it in the frontend.
- Check how the existing helper treats a plant with no waterings (for example due today, or based on a created date) and make sure a snooze extends that case the same way.
- Snooze base date (recommendation; see open questions): snoozed_until = max(today, current effective due date) + N days. Counting from the due date of an overdue plant would leave it still overdue, so 'snooze 1 day' would do nothing useful. Counting from the effective due date lets snoozes stack on an upcoming plant.
- Validation: days must be a positive integer within a sane upper bound (for example 1–365). Reject anything else with 400, using the API's existing error shape. Unknown plant id returns 404, matching the existing plant routes.
- Clearing on watering: set snoozed_until = NULL inside the same db.transaction as the watering insert in POST /api/plants/:id/waterings. better-sqlite3 transactions are synchronous. Clear it even if the watering is backdated, if the Waterings work allows backdating. Deleting a watering (DELETE /api/waterings/:id) should NOT restore a previous snooze; there's no history of snoozes.
- Plant edit: if the edit endpoint writes every column from the request body, make sure it keeps snoozed_until instead of setting it to NULL.
- Dates: the helper uses local calendar dates. Follow how Foundation computes 'today' (an injectable 'today' or clock parameter, if it has one) so tests are deterministic and don't depend on time zone or midnight. Format '<date>' in the UI the same way the rest of the app shows dates.
- UI: keep the calm, minimal style. On cards, '+1 day' should be one tap. The N-days choice can be a small number input or a few presets plus a custom value; avoid heavy modals. After setting or cancelling a snooze, refresh the data so the card moves between Overdue / Due today / Upcoming. Use real buttons with clear accessible labels.
- Tests required by the work order: (a) due helper cases: no snooze; snooze later than the normal due date (status and days follow the snooze, so an overdue plant moves to upcoming); snooze earlier than or equal to the normal due date (no effect); snooze in the past; null snoozed_until. (b) API: set a snooze for 1 and for N days, and the list/detail responses reflect it; cancel sets it to null; invalid days returns 400; unknown plant returns 404; POST watering clears snoozed_until. Also update any existing Foundation/Dashboard/Waterings tests whose expected response shape changes.
- Run tests with npm test at the repo root (Vitest in api/ and frontend/). Don't add new dependencies unless the existing test setup on main truly can't cover the UI.

**Left to settle**
- What date does a snooze count from? Recommended: max(today, current effective due date) + N days. The alternative, today + N, doesn't stack. Confirm against the existing helper's semantics.
- API shape: a dedicated snooze sub-resource (for example PUT/POST /api/plants/:id/snooze {days} and DELETE /api/plants/:id/snooze), or a PATCH on the plant. Pick whatever fits the route style on main.
- How the user picks N days on a card: a number input, presets (1/2/3/7) plus custom, or similar. Keep it small and consistent between the card and the detail page.

plan.statement: Plant Water Tracker is a small personal web app for one person who wants to keep their houseplants alive without remembering every schedule. guesses: One React page app served by one Node/Express server, with a SQLite database file kept in a named Docker volume.
The 30-plant catalog lives in a JSON seed file in the code. The server reads it directly, and it is never edited from the app.
Next due date = latest watering date + interval, or the snooze date if that is later. A plant with no waterings counts from the last-watered date set when it was added.
'Upcoming' lists every plant not yet due, sorted by soonest. It is not limited to a fixed number of days.
Undoing an accidental log is a short 'Undo' prompt right after tapping Watered. Older entries can be deleted from the history list.
Snoozing pushes only the current due date. The next real watering clears the snooze and the normal interval applies again.
Photos are optional, one per plant, limited to common image types and a reasonable size, and stored as files in the data volume.
Dates use the computer's local calendar day, with no times of day.

When a plant has no photo it shows a friendly leaf placeholder in the same spot, matching the existing 🌿 start-page style. Add API tests for upload, replace, remove and file cleanup (including on plant delete), plus frontend tests for the thumbnail/placeholder rendering. This builds on the "Manage plants with catalog picker" feature (plants table, plant CRUD routes, Add/Edit forms, detail page, home cards). That feature is not in main yet: main is only the scaffold. Fit into whatever structure it introduces.

**Where it changes**
- api/src/db.js: schema/migration adding nullable plants.photo_path TEXT (follow whatever migration approach the plants feature uses; it must also work on an existing DB that already has a plants table)
- api/src/app.js (or plant routes module from the dependency): photo upload/replace endpoint (multipart), remove endpoint, photo-serving GET route, file cleanup in plant DELETE; include photo URL or photo_path in plant JSON
- api/src/server.js: create DATA_DIR/photos and pass the photos directory into createApp (currently createApp(db) only)
- api/package.json + package-lock.json: add a multipart parser (e.g. multer), and optionally a HEIC converter
- api/src/*.test.js: tests for upload, replace, remove, rejects (wrong type/too big), serving, and cleanup on replace/remove/plant delete, using a temp photos dir
- frontend Add/Edit plant forms (from dependency): file input with preview, replace and remove controls, size/type validation messages; send the photo after or alongside the plant save
- frontend home plant card + Plant detail page: square thumbnail / larger image with leaf placeholder (a shared PlantPhoto component is a good fit)
- frontend/src/index.css: thumbnail/large photo/placeholder styles (object-fit: cover, square aspect)
- frontend tests: placeholder vs image rendering
- README.md: mention photos stored in api-data volume under photos/

**To keep in mind**
- Repo state checked on main: api/src/app.js exports createApp(db) with only GET /api/health and express.json(); db.js openDb(filename) enables WAL and foreign_keys and skips mkdir for ':memory:'; server.js uses DATA_DIR (compose sets /app/data on the api-data named volume) and opens DATA_DIR/plants.db. No plants table, routes or pages exist yet, so rebase onto or wait for the catalog-picker feature.
- Stack: Express 5.3 (async handler errors reach the error handler automatically; no multipart parsing built in), better-sqlite3 13 (synchronous), React 19 + Vite 8, Vitest 5, supertest. There is no router, jsdom or testing-library: frontend tests use react-dom/server renderToString in a node environment. Follow that pattern unless the dependency feature changed it.
- Make the photos directory injectable (e.g. createApp(db, { photosDir })) so tests use a fresh fs.mkdtemp dir with ':memory:' DB and can assert files appear and disappear.
- Security: generate filenames on the server (random UUID + extension from the detected type) and never use the client filename. Store only the relative path (e.g. photos/<uuid>.jpg) in photo_path, and resolve and confirm it stays inside photosDir before reading or deleting. Detect type from magic bytes, not just Content-Type or extension. Serve with the correct Content-Type and X-Content-Type-Options: nosniff. Reject anything else with 400 and oversize files with 413 (multer LIMIT_FILE_SIZE needs mapping to a friendly JSON error).
- Ordering and consistency: on replace, write the new file, update the DB row, then delete the old file. If the DB update fails, delete the new file. If deleting the old file fails, log it and don't fail the request. Treat a missing file as already deleted (ENOENT is fine). On plant delete, read photo_path before deleting the row and unlink afterwards. If multer writes to disk, make sure a rejected upload or an unknown plant id leaves no stray file (memoryStorage + validate + write avoids this; 10 MB in memory is fine for a single-user app).
- Caching: photo filenames change on every replace, so a URL that includes the filename or a version (e.g. /api/plants/:id/photo?v=<uuid> or /api/photos/<uuid>.jpg) avoids showing a stale image after replace.
- Docker: compose only bind-mounts api/src, and node_modules come from npm ci in the image. Adding an npm dependency means updating package-lock.json and rebuilding (docker compose up --build), so note this in the README or PR. The photos live inside the existing api-data volume, so compose needs no change.
- HEIC: Chrome, Firefox and Edge cannot display HEIC; only Safari can. Storing HEIC as-is would show broken images on most browsers. Sharp's prebuilt binaries do not decode HEVC-based HEIC. A pure-JS converter (e.g. heic-convert/libheif-js) could turn HEIC into JPEG on upload, but it is slow and heavy. iOS Safari usually converts HEIC to JPEG itself when picking from the photo library with accept='image/*'.
- UI: thumbnail square via aspect-ratio: 1 + object-fit: cover. Use alt text with the plant name, and give the placeholder role='img' with an aria-label or an aria-hidden decorative label. Keep the calm green theme from index.css. File input accept='image/jpeg,image/png,image/webp,image/heic,image/heif'. Check size on the client too, for faster feedback, but the server stays authoritative.
- Add form: the plant does not exist until it is saved, so either upload after the create response returns the id, or accept multipart on create. Pick one and keep Edit consistent. Remove should be a distinct action (e.g. DELETE /api/plants/:id/photo or a 'remove' flag) and should not happen just because the file input was left empty.
- Existing test to keep passing: api/src/app.test.js health test calls createApp(openDb(':memory:')), so any new createApp options need defaults or that test must be updated.

**Left to settle**
- HEIC support: (a) convert HEIC/HEIF to JPEG on the server with a pure-JS converter, which adds a heavy dependency, (b) reject HEIC with a friendly message and rely on iOS converting to JPEG itself, or (c) store HEIC as-is, accepting that it won't display outside Safari. Recommended: (a) if the dependency is acceptable, otherwise (b). Avoid (c).
- API shape: multipart on plant create/update, or a separate PUT/DELETE /api/plants/:id/photo sub-resource? The sub-resource is simpler to test and keeps the JSON plant endpoints unchanged. Settle this against how the dependency feature's routes and forms are built.
